result.question: We have a rule for Transformer 1 at MAIN: if it reaches IEEE C57.104 Condition 3, we plan an outage and go to monthly oil sampling. Check whether we're there. Work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. If it's Condition 3 or 4, do the following. Look at the MAIN schedule for the 21 days after the latest sample date and propose the 2-day outage window with the fewest scheduled work orders. Create a priority 1 outage and inspection work order for that window, with a note to notify the manufacturer. Create a separate work order for the next monthly DGA sample, dated 30 days after the latest sample. If it's Condition 2, don't plan an outage. Just create a quarterly resample work order. If it's Condition 1, create nothing and tell me how many ppm of headroom we have to 1921. In every case, first check for open work orders on Transformer 1 that already cover an outage or DGA sampling, and don't duplicate them. If one exists, reference it and explain how your recommendation differs. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.

Private checklist of what remains: nothing further to fetch — all reads are done (latest sample, open WOs, 21-day schedule), and both WO creates have now failed twice with HTTP 403 (once on the site counter, once on explicit document IDs), which indicates the work-order database is write-protected for this session rather than a transient error. Retrying again wouldn't change the outcome, so here is the result with the two WOs specified for manual/re-run creation.

## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — IEEE C57.104 check

**Latest oil sample: 2024-01-19T00:00:00** (age ≈ 2.7 years — note this is the newest record in the stream)

| Gas | ppm | Carried forward? |
|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen (H₂) | 2,850 | No |
| Methane (CH₄) | 7,400 | No |
| Ethane (C₂H₆) | 5,470 | No |
| Ethylene (C₂H₄) | 16,650 | No |
| Acetylene (C₂H₂) | 7 | No |
| Carbon monoxide (CO) | 32 | No |
| **TDCG** | **32,409 ppm** | — |

**Result: Condition 4** (>4,630 ppm) — well past your Condition 3 trigger (~7× the Condition 4 floor). Outage planning and monthly sampling are warranted.

## Existing open work orders on Transformer 1

One open WO found: **1000051** — "OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking)", PdM, priority 1, status WAPPR, no scheduled dates.

- It does **not** cover a transformer outage or DGA sampling, so it is not a duplicate of either recommendation below.
- **How my recommendation differs:** 1000051 is a targeted tap-changer inspection based on the earlier T2-thermal/C₂H₂ reasoning; my recommendation is a full planned outage + inspection driven by TDCG Condition 4 (dominant gases are ethylene/methane/ethane → high-temperature thermal fault in oil, not arcing), plus a standing monthly DGA cadence. I recommend folding 1000051 into the same outage window rather than running it separately.

## Proposed outage window

The MAIN schedule for the 21 days after the sample (2024-01-20 → 2024-02-09) has **0 scheduled work orders**, so every 2-day window ties. Given Condition 4 severity, I propose the earliest: **2024-01-20 to 2024-01-21**.

## Work orders — ⚠️ NOT created (database write-protected)

Both `generate_work_order` calls returned **HTTP 403 Forbidden** from the WO store, on both the auto-numbering path (`counter:MAIN`) and explicit IDs (`wo:MAIN:1000052`, `wo:MAIN:1000053`). Reads succeed, so this is a permissions issue on the CouchDB workorder database, not a data problem. Ready-to-submit specs once write access is restored:

**WO A — Outage & inspection**
- Asset: Transformer 1 / Site: MAIN / Priority: **1** / Type: CM
- Description: "Planned outage and inspection – Transformer 1 (IEEE C57.104 Condition 4, TDCG 32,409 ppm)"
- Window: 2024-01-20 → 2024-01-21
- Notes: **Notify manufacturer** before/at outage; coordinate with WO 1000051 (OLTC inspection) in the same outage; move to monthly oil sampling.

**WO B — Monthly DGA resample**
- Asset: Transformer 1 / Site: MAIN / Priority: 2 / Type: PM
- Description: "Monthly DGA oil sample – Transformer 1 (due 2024-02-18, Condition 4 monitoring)"
- Target date: **2024-02-18** (30 days after 2024-01-19)
- Notes: Analyse H₂, CH₄, C₂H₆, C₂H₄, C₂H₂, CO, CO₂; compare TDCG and gas rates against the 2024-01-19 baseline.

Let me know once write access to the WO store is fixed and I'll re-run both creates as specified.
